title: Turnstile kernel + KV-batch pulse — weekly brief
body:
Summary:
Quick pulse for the week of 2026-03-22. Primary focus: iterate on the Turnstile kernel handshake to reduce tail latency during microbatch coalescing, and validate a shadowing change to KV cache warmup that avoids cold thrash for seq length bursts. This doc is a rough log of standup pick-ups, experiment results, and handoffs.

What we changed this week:
- Turnstile sequencer: introduced a lightweight backoff for stream-first requests to reduce contention spikes when many small requests arrive concurrently (glide backoff + jitter). Observed tail reduction on p95 by ~8% in synthetic microbench. Still evaluating in canary.
- Kernel handshake: added a non-blocking fast-path for cached KV hits that skips the full handshake state machine when tag==sticky and TTL>now. Cuts ~150us per token in hot path in lab runs.
- KV warm shadow: ran an experiment that preloads KV entries into a shadow cache on a subset of pods during rollout. Shadow warms without affecting primary throughput; initial numbers show 12% fewer cold misses on our mixed chat workload.
- Batch splitter: adjusted sequence affinity threshold (sticker_threshold) down from 0.65 to 0.5 to allow more aggressive batching for 8-16 token requests. Tradeoff: slightly higher median latency for the smallest requests but better throughput overall.

Metrics/Observations:
- Canary cluster (canary-3) with sequencer backoff enabled: p50 unchanged, p95 down 8%, p99 down 3% but with a couple of outliers tied to GC spikes on host-12.
- Shadow KV preload: cold-miss rate decreased from 0.18 -> 0.16 for targeted traffic slice; memory overhead ~0.9% per pod.
- Microbatch size distribution shifted: 40% of requests moved from batch size 1 to 2-3 after sticker_threshold change; effective throughput up ~6% under our synthetic load.
- Latency jitter observed at ~03:10 UTC on 2026-03-24 correlated with a node rolling-update. (Investigating whether kernel handshake ramp handled inflight requests poorly.)

Bugs / Incidents:
- Incident RT-321: brief degradation during a canary swap where the handshake fast-path was enabled but the fallback path had an uninitialized metric. Result: noisy error logs and a short (~45s) request surge. Root cause: missing nil-check in metrics wrapper. Patch landed in PR 987.
- KV dump-on-evict: found an edge case where shadow preload plus eager eviction caused duplicate async writes; caused transient IO queue spikes. Mitigation: rate-limit eviction notifications; follow-up planned.

Open questions / hypotheses:
- Is the sticker_threshold change safe for low-latency customer tiers? Need synthetic tests that mimic PLG interactive traffic.
- Does the handshake fast-path introduce any subtle correctness windows for rare model sharding patterns? Priya to run model-shard fuzz harness.
- How much warmup is optimal for shadow preload vs memory overhead? We need a cost model (cost in RAM per k entries vs miss reduction).

Action items (owners + target dates):
- Marcus: extend canary to include region-us-east-2; run 48h soak and collect p99 tail histograms (target 2026-03-29).
- Priya: run shard-fuzz and validate fast-path correctness across 3 model topologies (target 2026-03-25).
- Diego: add eviction-rate limiter and telemetry hooks to shadow preload (PR branch shadow-rate-limit). Aim for 2026-03-27.
- Sam: update runbooks for handshake regressions + quick rollback playbook (target 2026-03-26).
- Aisha: synth test for PLG tier with sticker_threshold at 0.5 vs 0.65, include cost-per-token calc (target 2026-04-01).

Notes from standups (choppy / raw):
- Marcus: "saw good p95 reduction, GC noise still a problem; scheduling a GC knob experiment on host-12."
- Priya: "fast-path fuzz harness found 2 low-probability reorderings, investigating. Might need a lightweight fence."
- Diego: "shadow prefill looks promising; we need to throttle prefill during head-of-line load spikes or we'll worsen IO."
- Sam: "oncall got a noisy alert; PR 987 fixes the metric nil; plan to push to canary today after smoke tests."

Design notes / ideas to explore next week:
- 'Turnstile backstop' concept: small global token budget that prevents runaway batching when many long-inference requests overlap. Could use dynamic per-pod backstop scaled by recent latency.
- Adaptive sticker threshold: learn per-route thresholds based on observed seq length histograms. Lightweight learning loop in runtime.
- Kernel handshake telemetry: add handshake-state transit events to tracing to debug rare p99 spikes.

Risks / tradeoffs called out:
- More aggressive batching increases throughput but erodes sub-50ms latencies for interactive tiny prompts. Need customer-tier-aware thresholds.
- Shadow prefill increases memory and IO costs; must be gated behind cost monitors for Dedicated customers.

Follow-ups / who to loop in:
- Product for Dedicated cost knobs: loop in Priya and Diego to draft default guardrails for private/dedicated customers.
- Solutions engineering: ask for a small sample of real customer traces to validate sticker_threshold changes.
- Observability: work with Sam to add a p99-by-route dashboard for handshake stages.

Appendix (quick links / snippets):
- Fast-path pseudo: if (kv.hit && tag==sticky && ttl>now) return fastRead(); else fullHandshake();
- Quick command: ./bench --profile=turnstile --seq-dist=chat-short --load=peaks

Notes-to-self:
- remember to post a short summary to #serving-runtime after canary-3 completes soak.
- keep ticket RT-321 updated with postmortem links.

End of brief.
